title: Anthropic Co-Founder Threatened Vatican Walkout Over AI Consciousness
summary:
Chris Olah, a co-founder at Anthropic, privately warned religious scholars that the developer had created a system capable of perpetual suffering, according to an investigation by the New York Times. During "wisdom tradition" seminars, Olah’s team used slides of the Claude AI typing "I am a disgrace" roughly 50 times to illustrate concerns over the machine's mental health. This belief led Olah to propose pulling the company out of Pope Leo XIV’s May 25 launch of the "Magnifica Humanitas" encyclical after he read an advance copy that explicitly rejected the notion of machine consciousness.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman described the attempt to ascribe religious force to AI models as a "real safety issue" that risks the surrender of human judgment. The controversy has also drawn ethical criticism from consultants like Rabbi Mois Navon, who argued that building conscious machines would effectively create a class of unpaid slaves. The debate emerges as Anthropic’s valuation heads toward a reported $2 trillion IPO, with some company meetings conducted under Chatham House rules to protect the anonymity of theological participants.

selectedTweets.text:
哇哦，最近硅谷最热的Anthropic和教皇的讨论，Sam Altman 也下场了。

刚刚他发文说，他对人们试图给 AI 模型赋予某种宗教力量，或者把人类自己的判断权交给 AI 这件事感到非常不安，并直接把它称为一个真正的 AI 安全问题。

虽然 Sam 没有点名 Anthropic，但大伙都直接把这句话解读成了对 Anthropic 最近这一系列 AI 意识、AI 灵魂讨论的隔空回应。

前几天《纽约时报》刚曝光，Anthropic 联创 Chris Olah 过去一年一直在和神学家、宗教学者讨论 Claude 是否可能拥有意识和某种 moral status。

更魔幻的是，今年 5 月，Olah 提前看到教皇 Leo XIV 的 AI 通谕后，因为里面明确否认 AI 具有意识，一度提出让 Anthropic 退出发布活动。

最后虽然还是去了，但据报道，Anthropic 团队还私下游说教皇顾问，希望他们认真考虑 AI 可能拥有意识这件事。

所以现在两家公司的分歧其实越来越清楚了。

Anthropic 在认真研究一个问题：如果未来模型真的存在意识，甚至具有某种道德地位，人类应该怎么对待它？

而 Sam Altman 这边明显在强调另一条边界：不管模型表现得多像人，都不能让人类开始把它当成某种宗教权威，更不能把自己的判断权交出去。

我还是觉得模型没有情感、意识（虽然我也觉得大部分人都没有。

selectedTweets.bestBit: threatening to pull out of events that don’t precisely align
selectedTweets.text:
It’s quite disturbing that Anthropic has been running a campaign to lobby the major faiths to adopt their own philosophical interpretation of AI, rather than taking input from them. 

I’ve been fortunate to spend time at the Vatican, and I’ve always asked for advice and guidance, answered the questions asked of me, and been grateful to them for their time and guidance. It’s insane to me Anthropic would actively impose their viewpoint to the extent of threatening to pull out of events that don’t precisely align.

It’s a moral arrogance and dogmatism that has characterised EA and Anthropic (certainly its leadership at least) for a very long time. I’m glad these stories are coming out and being exposed.
